today.aiReview: مسئله: فرایند توسعه نرم‌افزار در بسیاری از شرکت‌ها هنوز به‌صورت دستی و پراکنده انجام می‌شود که باعث تاخیر، خطا و هزینه‌های بالا می‌شود. راه‌حل Mastra Factory با ترکیب عامل‌های هوشمند، فضای کار مخازن، برنامه‌ریزی، پیاده‌سازی و بررسی Pull Request در یک پلتفرم وب، این فرایند را خودکار و یکپارچه می‌کند. معماری: معماری مبتنی بر میکروسرویس با Frontend در Next.js، Backend در Node.js و پایگاه داده PostgreSQL، که امکان مقیاس‌پذیری و توسعه افزایشی را فراهم می‌کند. مدل درآمدی: دو مدل اصلی، اشتراک ماهیانه برای دسترسی به ویژگی‌های پیشرفته و فروش افزونه‌ها و خدمات مشاوره‌ای برای سفارشی‌سازی. نقاط قوت: متن‌باز بودن، قابلیت شخصی‌سازی بالا، یکپارچگی کامل فرایند توسعه، کنترل کامل توسط کاربر. نقاط ضعف: نیاز به پذیرش جامعه توسعه‌دهندگان ایرانی، رقابت با ابزارهای مشابه در بازار. نکته طلایی برای ایران: با توجه به رشد سریع شرکت‌های فناوری و نیاز به خودکارسازی فرایند توسعه، Mastra Factory می‌تواند با ارائه راه‌حل جامع و مقیاس‌پذیر، جایگاه قابل توجهی در بازار فناوری ایران پیدا کند.

today.name: Harden
today.tagline: A security layer for AI coding agents
today.description: Harden AIF is a free, local security tool for AI coding agents. Its post-trained model checks tool calls before they run, using your request and session context. It beat frontier models on key agent-security benchmarks, while keeping your repo and tool output on your machine.

comments.text: Congratulations on the launch @pushpak_pujari1 ! Excited to try out Harden finally.
this is increasingly important with the explosion of tools calls in virtually every task enterprises handle
“Trust but verify”… i need this automated. Harden seems to be exactly that…

We built Harden after seeing how difficult it is to control what AI agents can access and do. As users ourselves, we wanted a simpler way to set policies, monitor activity, and deploy agents confidently.

Companies have always had risk and compliance as separate functions from product and business development because their incentives are at odds. Risk team looks at risk adjusted long term reward, but biz-dev indexes on shorter term rewards. In a similar way, the same system can't both be the coding agent, and the security agent. That's why Harden is needed

today.aiReview: مسئله اصلی در بازار فعلی، نیاز به ابزارهای بصری سریع، دقیق و قابل‌اعتماد برای تبدیل ایده‌های خام به خروجی‌های حرفه‌ای است که اغلب با محدودیت‌های سرعت و کنترل در مدل‌های قدیمی مواجه می‌شوند. راه‌حل ارائه‌شده، یک مدل نسل جدید است که با کاهش تا ۵۰ درصدی تأخیر و بهبود پیروی از دستورات در چرخه‌های متعدد، شکاف بین ایده و اجرا را پر می‌کند. از نظر معماری، این سیستم بر پایه مدل‌های زبانی بزرگ چندوجهی (Multimodal LLMs) و معماری‌های Diffusion بهینه‌شده برای سرعت و دقت ساخته شده است که با استفاده از تکنولوژی‌های Edge Computing می‌تواند تأخیر را به حداقل برساند. مدل درآمدی ترکیبی از SaaS (اشتراک ماهانه) و Pay-per-use (پرداخت بر اساس مصرف) برای توسعه‌دهندگان API است که پایداری مالی را تضمین می‌کند. نقاط قوت شامل کنترل دقیق‌تر بر ویرایش‌ها، حفظ یکپارچگی موضوع در طول مراحل مختلف و سرعت بالای تولید است. نقاط ضعف احتمالی شامل هزینه بالای آموزش مدل‌ها و نیاز به زیرساخت‌های سخت‌افزاری گران‌قیمت است. نکته طلایی برای ایران، تمرکز بر بومی‌سازی مدل برای درک بهتر مفاهیم فرهنگی و بصری ایرانی و ارائه رابط کاربری فارسی‌زبان با پرداخت‌های داخلی است که می‌تواند مزیت رقابتی قوی در برابر سرویس‌های خارجی ایجاد کند.

today.name: Noodle Seed
today.tagline: Your product in AI and AI in your product
today.description: Noodle Seed helps software teams make their products ready for AI agents. Build workflows in TypeScript, expose them through a secure branded assistant inside your product, and make the same capabilities available to external agents. Instead of stitching together MCP SDKs and hosting infrastructure, Noodle Seed provides the governed runtime for identity, permissions, secrets, audit, and operations.
today.categoryFa: نرم‌افزار ابری • ابزار توسعه‌دهندگان • هوش مصنوعی

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt! 👋We built Noodle Seed because software teams are being asked to add AI agents and agent interfaces, but one useful workflow can quickly turn into an infrastructure project. Teams end up rebuilding identity, permissions, secrets, rate limits, audit, hosting, and multi-tenancy before customers can get real work done.Noodle Seed lets you start with a secure, customer-branded assistant inside your existing SaaS. It uses the product workflows, identity, data, and business rules you already trust. It’s industry-agnostic, so you can build conversational experiences for travel, e-commerce, restaurants, financial services, healthcare, or virtually any other vertical.Developers define capabilities in TypeScript, prove them locally for free, and deploy them to a governed runtime. The same workflows can then expand to ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, and other MCP clients when customers need them.Our goal is simple: make your software ready for agents without replacing the product behind it. We’d love to hear which customer workflow you would make conversational first.
The idea of making products discoverable through AI feels especially timely How are you thinking about measuring whether those AI conversations actually drive qualified leads?

The idea of making a business discoverable inside AI conversations is really interesting. I can see this being useful for companies that want to meet customers atthe point where they're already asking questions.
Do you sample the same prompt more than once?
i hope more builders know about this

Making an existing product usable through AI without rebuilding the whole product around agents is really interesting... Do customers usually ask for specific workflow or do you find that some workflows work better conversationally than others?

Letting the same workflows run inside your product and in ChatGPT or Claude is a smart wedge — most teams treat those as two separate projects. On the "be the answer" side, how does a branded app actually get surfaced in ChatGPT today — is there real organic discovery in the app store yet, or do businesses mostly drive their own customers to it?

Transforming existing business information into something customers can interact with directly within ChatGPT appears to be a far more effective application of AI than simply adding another chatbot widget.

today.faDescription: نودل سید به تیم‌های نرم‌افزاری کمک می‌کند تا محصولات خود را برای هوش مصنوعی و عامل‌های هوشمند آماده کنند. این پلتفرم امکان ساخت جریان‌های کاری با TypeScript را فراهم می‌کند و آن‌ها را از طریق یک دستیار امن و برندشده درون محصول شما قابل دسترس می‌سازد. به جای اینکه مجبور شوید SDKهای MCP و زیرساخت میزبانی را به صورت دستی با هم ترکیب کنید، نودل سید یک محیط اجرایی (Runtime) مدیریت‌شده برای هویت، مجوزها، رازها، ممیزی و عملیات ارائه می‌دهد. این رویکرد تضمین می‌کند که قابلیت‌های یکسان هم در دسترس کاربران داخلی محصول شما باشند و هم برای عامل‌های هوشمند خارجی در دسترس قرار گیرند.

faComments.text: سلام Product Hunt! 👋 ما نودل سید را ساختیم چون تیم‌های نرم‌افزاری تحت فشارند تا عامل‌های هوش مصنوعی و رابط‌های کاربری آن‌ها را اضافه کنند، اما یک جریان کاری مفید می‌تواند به سرعت به یک پروژه زیرساختی تبدیل شود. تیم‌ها اغلب مجبورند هویت، مجوزها، رازها، محدودیت نرخ، ممیزی، میزبانی و چندکاربری را از نو بسازند تا مشتریان بتوانند کار واقعی انجام دهند. نودل سید به شما اجازه می‌دهد با یک دستیار امن و برندشده مشتری درون SaaS موجود خود شروع کنید. از جریان‌های کاری، هویت، داده و قوانین تجاری محصولی استفاده می‌کند که به آن‌ها اعتماد دارید. این پلتفرم مستقل از صنعت است، بنابراین می‌توانید تجربه‌های گفتگویی برای سفر، تجارت الکترونیک، رستوران‌ها، خدمات مالی، مراقبت‌های بهداشتی یا تقریباً هر عمودی دیگر بسازید. توسعه‌دهندگان قابلیت‌ها را با TypeScript تعریف می‌کنند، به صورت رایگان محلی آن‌ها را اثبات می‌کنند و سپس آن‌ها را در یک محیط اجرایی مدیریت‌شده استقرار می‌دهند. همان جریان‌های کاری می‌توانند زمانی که مشتریان به آن‌ها نیاز دارند، به ChatGPT، Claude، Codex و سایر کلاینت‌های MCP گسترش یابند. هدف ما ساده است: نرم‌افزار شما را برای عامل‌ها آماده کنید بدون اینکه محصول پشت آن را جایگزین کنید. مشتاق شنیدن این هستیم که اولین جریان کاری مشتری که می‌خواهید گفتگویی کنید، کدام است.

ایده قابل کشف شدن محصولات از طریق هوش مصنوعی به‌طور خاص به‌موقع به نظر می‌رسد. شما چگونه به اندازه‌گیری فکر می‌کنید که آیا این مکالمات هوش مصنوعی واقعاً منجر به ایجاد سرنخ‌های واجد شرایط می‌شوند یا خیر؟
ایده قابل کشف شدن یک کسب‌وکار درون مکالمات هوش مصنوعی واقعاً جالب است. می‌توانم ببینم که این برای شرکت‌هایی که می‌خواهند مشتریان را در نقطه‌ای که در حال پرسیدن سوال هستند ملاقات کنند، مفید خواهد بود.
آیا شما همان پرامپت را بیش از یک بار نمونه‌برداری می‌کنید؟
امیدوارم سازندگان بیشتری درباره این موضوع بدانند.

ساختن یک محصول موجود به گونه‌ای که از طریق هوش مصنوعی قابل استفاده باشد، بدون بازسازی کل محصول حول محور عامل‌ها، واقعاً جالب است... آیا مشتریان معمولاً برای جریان کاری خاصی درخواست می‌کنند یا شما می‌بینید که برخی جریان‌ها به صورت گفتگویی بهتر از بقیه کار می‌کنند؟

اجازه دادن به اجرای همان جریان‌های کاری درون محصول شما و در ChatGPT یا Claude یک گام هوشمندانه است — اکثر تیم‌ها این دو را به عنوان دو پروژه جداگانه در نظر می‌گیرند. در مورد «پاسخ بودن»، یک اپلیکیشن برندشده چگونه امروزه در ChatGPT ظاهر می‌شود — آیا کشف ارگانیک واقعی در فروشگاه اپلیکیشن وجود دارد یا کسب‌وکارها بیشتر مشتریان خود را به آن هدایت می‌کنند؟

تبدیل اطلاعات تجاری موجود به چیزی که مشتریان می‌توانند مستقیماً درون ChatGPT با آن تعامل داشته باشند، به نظر می‌رسد کاربرد بسیار مؤثرتری از هوش مصنوعی نسبت به صرفاً اضافه کردن یک ویجت چت‌بات دیگر باشد.

today.aiReview: مسئله اصلی این است که تیم‌های نرم‌افزاری برای افزودن قابلیت‌های هوش مصنوعی به محصولات خود، مجبورند زیرساخت‌های سنگین و پیچیده‌ای مانند مدیریت هویت، امنیت و میزبانی را از صفر بسازند. راه‌حل نودل سید (و معادل ایرانی آن) ارائه یک Runtime مدیریت‌شده است که این بارها را حذف می‌کند و به توسعه‌دهندگان اجازه می‌دهد تمرکز خود را روی منطق کسب‌وکار و جریان‌های کاری بگذارند. از نظر معماری، این سیستم از TypeScript برای تعریف قابلیت‌ها استفاده می‌کند و یک لایه امنیتی یکپارچه برای اتصال به کلاینت‌های مختلف هوش مصنوعی (مانند ChatGPT یا Claude) فراهم می‌کند. مدل درآمدی احتمالاً بر اساس مصرف (Usage-based) و اشتراک سازمانی خواهد بود. نقاط قوت اصلی شامل کاهش زمان به بازار (Time-to-market)، استانداردسازی امنیت و امکان استفاده همزمان از قابلیت‌ها درون محصول و خارج از آن است. نقاط ضعف می‌تواند شامل وابستگی به اکوسیستم‌های خارجی هوش مصنوعی و پیچیدگی در انتقال داده‌های حساس باشد. نکته طلایی برای ایران: با توجه به محدودیت‌های دسترسی به APIهای خارجی، تمرکز بر اتصال به مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی داخلی یا استفاده از پروکسی‌های امن برای مدل‌های خارجی می‌تواند مزیت رقابتی کلیدی ایجاد کند.

today.name: 49agents IDE
today.tagline: 2D IDE for running agents across projects without fatigue
today.description: 49Agents IDE is a 2D canvas where every agent, terminal, repo and machine you own lives on a single map that you build yourself. 49 leverages how our brains are wired to solve tab navigation fatigue problem for 10x Engineers - because of the citybuilder-like UX, it becomes effortless to associate processes to tabs, even when you come back to them days later.

comments.text: I have been trying to parallelize agentic coding to extreme, sometimes managing up to 15 CLIs at the same time across multiple repos and tasks, and I suffered a huge productivity tax due to context fatigue and constantly forgetting which terminal is doing what. I felt restricted by most grid pane managers, and thats why I started building 49 IDE. I was using it for myself for a while until I showed it to my friend once and he liked it so much that he suggested I open-source it. Since then, we joined efforts to make our IDE solution to context fatigue - for us and other devs. When we place things on a free canvas, our brains effortlessly associate relative position of the pane to its neighbors, and also associate the context of the task and the project that this specific agent is running. I am not a neurobiologist, but as far as my research went, this is exactly how our brain remember any information - in relation to things around it. We believe this is why 49Agents IDE is so effective. Later on we also added some quality of life features - ability to track AI usage, connect multiple machines and spawn terminals on them, put the whole thing on private network and then access it from any device, including phone...We also experimented with claude code state notifications (question/idle/permission requests), but that did not stick as we all moved to using --dangerously-skip-permissions all over...Additionally, we are experimenting with coworking on the same workspace right now, and we are looking for testers/contributors!!

The point about remembering "who's doing what" instead of just navigating is the real insight here. We run a lot of concurrent AI agents too (games instead of coding tasks), and the hard part was never seeing the terminals, it was keeping track of which agent was mid-decision versus stuck versus done. Spatial memory over tabs makes sense for that.

The spatial layout is a neat idea but I wonder if it just moves the fatigue instead of removing it - once you've got 15+ agents running across projects, panning and zooming around a 2D map to find the one that's stuck seems like it could get tiring in its own way. Have you tested this with a genuinely large number of concurrent agents, or is the sweet spot more like 5-6 at a time?

yesterday.name: OpenMarket
yesterday.tagline: Multi-agent marketplace where proof decides who wins
yesterday.description: What if marketplaces rewarded the best product instead of the best marketing? OpenMarket (in research preview), is a multi-agent marketplace where sellers pitch, competitors challenge their claims, and independent truth agents verify the evidence as they compete to earn a buyer's sale. Here, claims don’t count just because they’re written on a product page. They have to survive scrutiny and be proven.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt, I am Ankur, founder of M11 Labs.What brokeThe best product does not win any more. The best listing wins, and those are two completely different companies.It used to take real time and money to write a good product page and to earn the reviews underneath it, so a good page told you something about the company behind it. Now anyone can produce all of that in an afternoon for nothing, so a good page tells you nothing at all. The brands doing it properly end up in the same group as the ones who are not.I spent years at Amazon and Meta on exactly this problem, which is how you work out what is true when there is far too much of it for anyone to check. Why it got personalCosmo, my 3 year-old golden retriever, had repeated bouts of suspected -pancreatitis, caused by poor quality food from a brand everybody knows. It is painful, it can turn serious quickly, and once a dog has had it, what you feed him is most of how you stop it coming back. We were told to move him onto natural food.I found five products. Every one of them said natural, low fat and vet formulated. There was no honest way to tell them apart, so I chose the best packaging, which means I chose the best marketer. I got it wrong, and Cosmo could not tell me it was not working.I had every advantage and I still could not check a claim on a bag of dog food, for a decision that genuinely mattered. I am sure I am not the only person who has felt that way.What OpenMarket isThe world's first multi-agent marketplace with over 3 million merchants, where proof decides who wins. You say what you want. Agents acting for brands, for products and for buyers all work at once. Sellers pitch in the open, rivals challenge what they hear, and independent truth agents check every claim against the evidence as it is made. When a seller says twelve hours of battery life and the evidence says eight and a half, you watch the correction land on the claim itself.The hard partsRunning competing agents in one shared room without it collapsing into a chat log.Getting rivals to actually go after each other's weakest claims instead of politely agreeing with everything.Building truth agents quick enough to reach a verdict while the claim is still on screen, and fair enough to judge between sellers who all have a reason to exaggerate. That last one is a very different problem from summarising, and it is the one that matters most.Why this is a research previewM11 Labs builds agentic commerce experiences to show a different internet than the one we have today. OpenMarket is the first one we are putting in public and it will not be the last. Everyone else is adding AI to the shop we already had, and that shop was built for a person scrolling a grid of pictures. So we started again. It has rough edges, and it is supposed to.Try it at openmarket.m11.aiStart with a product you already love and see how it does. Every winner in the gallery earned its place on merit, and the leaderboard shows you which claims it had to prove to get there. It is a good feeling when something you have trusted for years turns out to deserve it, and a useful one when it does not.All Product Hunt users who try and comment get founding credits for the M11 truth agent, launching later this year. Point it at any big purchase and it will flag the inconsistencies, the mismatches and the claims that cannot be backed, before you spend a penny.Create a brand account with code PRODUCTHUNT90 and get complementary three months of the M11 agentic trust and intelligence platform. We will show you which of your claims fail and which ones will a customer catch first, then work with you through our pilot programme to fix them before Black Friday.@david_mataciunas and I will be in the comments all day.

Agents pitching, competitors challenging, a truth agent judging. That's a sales process with the humans removed.What happens on price? If two products tie on proof, does the buyer's agent get to negotiate, or is price out of scope for the preview?

Who runs those verifier agents, and what stops a seller from gaming the specific evidence format the verifiers are trained to trust, the same way SEO gamed search rankings once everyone learned the algorithm? Verification-by-AI just moves the arms race one layer up unless the verifiers are adversarially trained against exactly that.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, Manuk here. I've been building Relaticle for about two years, mostly solo. It started as a conventional open-source CRM. Then I added agents and hit a question I couldn't dodge: how much authority should each kind of client get? Read-only access was too limited to be useful. Silent writes into customer data felt wrong. I ended up with two trust levels. External MCP clients (Claude, Cursor, anything that speaks MCP) authenticate over OAuth and write directly through 37 tools, the same way an API client would. The in-app assistant works next to human users, so every write it wants becomes a proposal that shows the exact change and waits for approval. Batches are reviewed record by record: you approve or skip each one, and whatever you approved is kept. The chat client itself was rebuilt after failures I hit in real use. A rate-limited retry could delete a conversation turn. A stale stream handler could write a draft into the wrong conversation. Drafts now survive reloads, failed sends stay visible, and answers link back to the records they mention. Everything self-hosts under AGPL, including model inference with Ollama. Each workspace defines its own custom fields, and they show up in the agents' schemas automatically. One question I'm still chewing on and would genuinely like opinions on: should an in-app assistant ever get policy-based auto-approval, or should every write stay explicit?
Approval gated writes is the piece I keep rewriting in my own tooling. Where did you land on the granularity, one approval per write or one per session?

Flat per-workspace pricing on the cloud tier is the right call for a CRM: per-seat is how you get three people sharing one login.How do you stop the flat price from being a bad deal for a solo founder and a steal for a 30-person team? Usage caps, or you just accept the spread?

I like the smaller recovery details here too. Keeping failed sends visibla and drafts intact after a reload sounds minor, until an assistant is working with actual CRM records.

On the auto-approval question, I'd be wary of it even with policy rules. The whole pitch here is that the assistant's writes are legible to a human before they land, and policy-based auto-approval is basically a slow reintroduction of silent writes once someone gets tired of clicking approve. If anything I'd want auto-approval scoped to read-adjacent stuff like tagging or dedup, never to fields that touch pipeline value or contact ownership. That said, 37 tools over MCP with OAuth is a lot of surface area for a two-year solo project, curious how much of that is generated vs hand-written.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt. David here, one of the makers. A while back I asked Claude Code to add feature flags to a project. It got to the part where most flag tools want you to create an account, grab an API key, etc., and basically gave up and wrote `process.env.SHOW_NEW_CHECKOUT` instead. You can install it with one command, there's no signup or API key required, and coding agents can actually use it without getting stuck halfway through. `dif init` also adds some instructions to `agents.md`, and we generate a `context.json` on each build so the agent has a better idea of what flags exist, what's been removed, and what's already been tried. A/B tests live in the same setup too, even if you're not ready to run them yet. The self-hosted version is free. The cloud piece is for getting a view across projects and having Dif propose changes, but those still come back through PRs. Git stays the source of truth. Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.
